title: A 45-minute screen leaves twenty-five minutes to code
takeaway: The compression is the difficulty: clarify fast, narrate the whole time, and test before you say done.
sources: It is usually 45 minutes, usually one problem, usually with someone who has your resume open and four other screens booked that day.

Twenty-five minutes of coding is not long, and it is why the first five minutes matter disproportionately: five minutes spent clarifying is fine, five minutes spent silently reading is a quarter of your coding time gone.
So the rule for this round specifically is: narrate more than feels natural.

lines.note: Clarifying is fine; silent reading eats coding time
Narrate every decision and every long pause
